precepts.text: No man might buy or sell save he that had the mark; Tobit losing all his goods for burying his brethren is the picture of what the system does to those who will not go along with it.
precepts.point: His nephew Achiacharus rose to be cupbearer, keeper of the signet and steward under Sarchedonus, spoke for him, and Tobit returned to Nineveh; he had looked out for his people and the Lord had his own look out for him.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Tobit had a decent job in captivity, over the king’s accounts, and while he was well off he did good: “I gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry, And my clothes to the naked”. When Sennacherib came back from Judea, where an angel killed 185,000 of his men, he came back mad and took it out on Ephraim, throwing them off the walls. Tobit would sneak and bury them: “I buried them privily”. He was not supposed to; the king wanted to see those bodies, “but the bodies were not found, when they were sought for of the king.”

Then he got ratted out: “when one of the Ninevites went and complained of me to the king, that I buried them”, he knew he “was sought for to be put to death” and became a fugitive. “Then all my goods were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, beside my wife Anna and my son Tobias.” Everything he had, they took from him.

That is what Revelation 13 means when it says no man should buy or sell. All the positions and things you have here: the time is going to come when you go against this system, teach against it, and do not support the beast, and everything you have they will take from you. Tobit is the example. They took his possessions, and most likely his wife and child were taken too, imprisoned, because he was considered an enemy of the state. That is the consequence for serving God, and the time is coming when you will have to make the choice to serve God.

But the Lord spared his son and wife. Within fifty-five days Sennacherib’s own sons killed him, and Sarchedonus set Tobit’s nephew Achiacharus over the accounts. “And Achiacharus intreating for me, I returned to Nineve.” His nephew was cupbearer, “keeper of the signet, and steward, and overseer of the accounts”, next unto the king, and he spoke for his uncle. Then “my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost”: he was keeping the feasts in captivity, not in Jerusalem.

Tobit stayed faithful, and he was not alone out there being righteous. He looked out for his people with the status he had, fed the hungry and gave alms to those keeping the commandments in captivity, and when it came back around his nephew did the same for him. The Lord looked out for him as he looked out for his own people.

precepts.text: Tobit walked in truth and justice and did many alms deeds to his brethren in captivity.
precepts.point: Tobit of Naphtali, carried captive to Nineveh, gave alms and buried his brethren whom Sennacherib killed in his rage after fleeing Judea.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Sennacherib came against Hezekiah and mocked his God, and one angel of the Lord went forth and smote “in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.” One angel killed 185,000 soldiers in their sleep. Judah was saved without bow or sword, just as Hosea said. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh”, and his own sons smote him with the sword while he worshipped in the house of Nisroch his god. He went home pissed off, and Tobit shows what he did.

Tobit was “of the tribe of Nephthali”, led captive in the time of Enemessar, which is the Greek form of Shalmaneser the fifth, out of “Nephthali in Galilee above Aser.” He is northern kingdom, carried to Nineveh. “I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the ways of truth and justice, and I did many almsdeeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineve, into the land of the Assyrians.”

“The most High gave me grace and favour before Enemessar, so that I was his purveyor”, overseeing the food and rations. When Enemessar died, Sennacherib his son reigned, the same Sennacherib that attacked Hezekiah and lost 185,000 men. Tobit “gave my bread to the hungry, and my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him.” Assyria was very brutal and vicious; they would take Israelites to the top of the walls and throw them off, and Tobit would bury his brothers broken in pieces on the ground.

“And if the king Sennacherib had slain any, when he was come, and fled from Judea, I buried them privily; for in his wrath he killed many.” Why did he flee from Judea? Because he lost 185,000 men. He was mad that he could not overthrow Judah, so out of anger he started killing Ephraim. When a Ninevite complained of Tobit to the king, his goods were forcibly taken away, and “there passed not five and fifty days, before two of his sons killed him”, the same death Isaiah 37:38 records.

Then Sarchedonus, Esarhaddon, reigned and appointed Achiacharus, Tobit's brother's son, over all his father's accounts, so Tobit gained standing again through his nephew. So Isaiah shows the angel saving Judah, and Tobit shows the other side of that same day: the northern kingdom in captivity in Nineveh, bearing Sennacherib's wrath, and a faithful Naphtalite burying his brethren.

precepts.text: Tobit lived in Nineveh in this same time, burying the Israelites Sennacherib slew.
precepts.point: Sennacherib departs and dwells at Nineveh, and as he worships in the house of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer smite him with the sword and flee, and Esarhaddon his son reigns in his stead, fulfilling the word of verse 7.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

precepts.why:
Tobit lived in Nineveh in this same time: “if the king Sennacherib had slain any, when he was come, and fled from Judea, I buried them privily; for in his wrath he killed many.”

Sennacherib fled from Judea after the angel of the Lord smote his camp, and returned to dwell at Nineveh, and there in his wrath he slew many Israelites. Tobit buried them in secret. When a Ninevite complained of him to the king, he hid himself for fear of death, “Then all my goods were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, beside my wife Anna and my son Tobias.”

precepts.text: Tobit records the same murder of Sennacherib by his sons and the reign of Esarhaddon, confirming the history of Kings.
precepts.point: Sennacherib departs and dwells at Nineveh, and as he worships in the house of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer smite him with the sword and flee, and Esarhaddon his son reigns in his stead, fulfilling the word of verse 7.

note.label: 2 Kings 19: The Most High Defends Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“And there passed not five and fifty days, before two of his sons killed him, and they fled into the mountains of Ararath; and Sarchedonus his son reigned in his stead.”

Tobit records the same murder of Sennacherib by his sons that Kings gives: “Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword: and they escaped into the land of Armenia. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.” Sarchedonus is Esarhaddon. Two witnesses to one history, and the word of verse 7 fulfilled.

precepts.text: Tobit, of the tribe of Nephthali in the northern kingdom, was carried captive to Nineveh yet still walked in truth and went up to Jerusalem, a remnant keeping the law like Cornelius.
precepts.point: Cornelius specifically was of the northern kingdom of Israel; the word was sent unto the children of Israel, and Cornelius was a just man giving alms and keeping the commandments even while scattered.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
Cornelius was not the first of the northern kingdom to keep the law while scattered. Tobit was “of the tribe of Nephthali; Who in the time of Enemessar king of the Assyrians was led captive out of Thisbe.”

“I Tobit have walked all the days of my life in the ways of truth and justice, and I did many almsdeeds to my brethren, and my nation, who came with me to Nineve, into the land of the Assyrians.” When the tribe of Nephthali fell from the house of Jerusalem and “sacrificed unto the heifer Baal”, Tobit said, “But I alone went often to Jerusalem at the feasts, as it was ordained unto all the people of Israel by an everlasting decree.”

Tobit, of the northern kingdom, carried captive to Nineveh, still walked in truth and went up to Jerusalem. He was a remnant keeping the law, and Cornelius is the same: a man of the scattered north, giving alms and keeping the commandments.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Tobit lived through the northern kingdom's cutting off. “all the tribe of Nephthali my father fell from the house of Jerusalem, which was chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, that all the tribes should sacrifice there, where the temple of the habitation of the most High was consecrated and built for all ages. Now all the tribes which together revolted, and the house of my father Nephthali, sacrificed unto the heifer Baal.”

“But I alone went often to Jerusalem at the feasts, as it was ordained unto all the people of Israel by an everlasting decree”, bringing the firstfruits and tenths to the priests the children of Aaron. Tobit alone kept going up; the tribes that revolted were away from the sacrifice at Jerusalem. That is the northern kingdom, strangers from the covenants, who could never be saved if salvation required animal sacrifice.
